definitions.explanation: Standard first-person plural pronoun. Polite enough for most situations: classroom, workplace, and public-facing speech. Inclusive when the listener is part of the group; otherwise refers to the speaker and others.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}たちは{学生|がくせい}です。
{日本|にほん}の{文化|ぶんか}は{私|わたし}たちの{誇|ほこ}りだ。
{今度|こんど}の{週末|しゅうまつ}、{私|わたし}たちは{京都|きょうと}に{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}く{予定|よてい}です。
examples.english: We're planning to travel to Kyoto this coming weekend.

notes:
Standard plural of {私|わたし} (I). Politeness-neutral and safe in nearly any context. Choice of first-person plural depends on speaker register and group composition.

FIRST-PERSON PLURALS:
- {私|わたし}たち: we (standard, neutral)
- {私|わたくし}たち: we (very formal)
- {僕|ぼく}たち / {僕|ぼく}ら: we (masculine, casual to neutral)
- {俺|おれ}たち / {俺|おれ}ら: we (masculine, casual/rough)
- うちら: we (feminine, casual)
- {我々|われわれ}: we (formal speeches, in-group identity)

USAGE:
- INCLUSIVE: includes the listener when context allows ({私|わたし}たちで{決|き}めよう Let's decide together).
- EXCLUSIVE: excludes the listener in most narrative contexts ({私|わたし}たちは{昨日|きのう}{映画|えいが}を{見|み}に{行|い}きました We went to a movie yesterday).

COMMON PATTERNS:
The possessive is {私|わたし}たちの (our). たち can attach to other personal nouns to mean 'and others' ({先生|せんせい}たち the teachers).
